arxiv-2002-10021.title: How Transferable are the Representations Learned by Deep Q Agents?
arxiv-2002-10021.creator: Jacob Tyo & Zachary Lipton
arxiv-2002-10021.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the source of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)’s sample complexity, asking how much derives from the requirement of learning useful representations of environment states and how much is due to the sample complexity of learning a policy.

arxiv-2105-05700.title: Baryogenesis from a CP-violating inflation Journal: BSM
arxiv-2105-05700.creator: Venus Keus
arxiv-2105-05700.description: Abstract We introduce the novel phenomena of CP-violating inflation in the frameworks of a 3-Higgs doublet model where the inflaton doublets have a non-minimal coupling to gravity. We allow for this coupling to be complex, thereby introducing CP-violation - a necessary source of the baryon asymmetry - in the inflaton couplings.

arxiv-2203-13041.title: Simulating realistic screening clouds around quantum impurities: role of spatial anisotropy and disorder
arxiv-2203-13041.creator: Maxime Debertolis, Izak Snyman, Serge Florens
arxiv-2203-13041.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Maxime Debertolis, Izak Snyman, Serge Florens. Dynamical quantum impurities in metals induce electronic correlations in real space that are difficult to simulate due to their multi-scale nature, so that only s-wave scattering in clean metallic hosts has been investigated so far. However, screening clouds should show anisotropy due to lack of full rotational invariance in two- and three-dimensional lattices, while inherent disorder will also induce spatial inhomogeneities.

arxiv-2212-00164.title: Possible existence of stable compact stars in κ ⁡ ( ℛ , 𝒯 ) − \kappa(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{T})- gravity
arxiv-2212-00164.creator: G R P Teruel, Ksh. Newton Singh, Farook Rahaman, Tanmoy chowdhury
arxiv-2212-00164.description: Abstract We present the first interior solutions representing compact stars in κ ⁡ ( ℛ , 𝒯 ) \kappa(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{T}) gravity, by solving the modified field equations in isotropic coordinates. Further, we have assumed the metric potentials in Schwarzschild’s form and a few parameters along with the isotropic condition of pressure.

arxiv-2312-09258.title: Comparative study of Kondo effect in Vanadium dichalcogenides VX 2 (X=Se & Te)
arxiv-2312-09258.creator: Indrani Kar, Susanta Ghosh, Shuvankar Gupta, Sudip Chakraborty, S. Thirupathaiah*
arxiv-2312-09258.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Indrani Kar, Susanta Ghosh, Shuvankar Gupta, Sudip Chakraborty, S. Thirupathaiah*. We report on the electrical transport, magnetotransport, and magnetic properties studies on the transition metal dichalcogenides VSe 2 and VTe 2 and draw a comprehensive comparison between them. We observe Kondo effect in both systems induced by the exchange interaction between localized moments and conduction electrons at low temperature, resulting into resistance upturn at 6 K for VSe 2 and 17 K for VTe 2 .

arxiv-2403-06298.title: Analysis of Total Variation Minimization for Clustered Federated Learning Thanks: This work has been supported by the Research Council of Finland under funding decision nr. 349966 349966 and 331197 331197 .
arxiv-2403-06298.creator: Alexander Jung
arxiv-2403-06298.description: Abstract A key challenge in federated learning applications is the statistical heterogeneity of local datasets. Clustered federated learning addresses this challenge by identifying clusters of local datasets that are approximately homogeneous. One recent approach to clustered federated learning is generalized total variation minimization (GTVMin).

arxiv-2504-13852.title: A Pandemic for the Good of Digital Literacy? An Empirical Investigation of Newly Improved Digital Skills during COVID-19 Lockdowns CCS: Social and professional topics User characteristics CCS: Applied computing Sociology CCS: Human-centered computing
arxiv-2504-13852.creator: German Neubaum, Irene-Angelica Chounta, Eva Gredel, David Wiesche
arxiv-2504-13852.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by German Neubaum, Irene-Angelica Chounta, Eva Gredel, David Wiesche. This research explores whether the rapid digital transformation due to COVID-19 managed to close or exacerbate the digital divide concerning users’ digital skills. We conducted a pre-registered survey with N = 1,143 German Internet users. Our findings suggest the latter: younger, male, and higher educated users were more likely to improve their digital skills than older, female, and less educated ones.

arxiv-2505-01818.creator: Ahrar N. Hamad, Ahmad Adnan Qidan, Taisir E.H. El-Gorashi and Jaafar M. H. Elmirghani
arxiv-2505-01818.description: Abstract Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) have emerged as a promising solution to mitigate line-of-sight (LoS) blockages and enhance signal coverage in optical wireless communication (OWC) systems with minimal additional power. In this work, we consider a mirror-based IRS to assist a dynamic indoor visible light communication (VLC) environment.

pmc-10667751.title: The pentalogy of Cantrell: A rare and challenging prenatal diagnosis
pmc-10667751.creator: Fathi Mraihi, Jihene Basly, Amani Mezni, Zeineb Ghali, Montasar Hafsi, Dalenda Chelli
pmc-10667751.description: IntroductionThe sternum, pericardium, diaphragm, abdominal wall, and heart are all affected by the unusual congenital condition known as Cantrell pentalogy. It is a rare congenital disorder that requires multidisciplinary care. Early diagnosis and appropriate management are crucial for improving outcomes in affected individuals. To illustrate the difficulties and complexity of Cantrell pentalogy, we provide two cases.

pmc-11614947.title: A narrative overview of undergraduate geriatric medicine education worldwide
pmc-11614947.creator: Grace M E Pearson, Yoav Ben-Shlomo, Emily J Henderson
pmc-11614947.description: There is a mismatch between the healthcare needs of the ageing population worldwide and the amount of education medical students receive in geriatric medicine. In 2014, Mateos-Nozal et al. published a systematic review of all undergraduate education surveys in geriatric medicine—a decade on, it is timely for an up-to-date overview of the state of undergraduate geriatric medicine education globally.

pmc-12444374.title: Addressing food system determinants of health inequalities in urban environments: learnings from the FoodSEqual and FoodSEqual-Health projects
pmc-12444374.creator: Carol Wagstaff, Clare Pettinger, Clare Relton, Katerina Psarikidou, Elaine Swan, Lisa Methven, Gunter Kuhnle, Rachel McCloy, Sally Lloyd-Evans, Michelle Thomas, Manik Puranik, Martin Chadwick, Lorna Zischka, Rachel Smith, Hannah Gardiner, Louise Hunt, Jiang Pan, Jane Bradbeer, Rachel Sutton, Barbara
pmc-12444374.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Diet is just one social determinant of health, with obesity and diet-related illness as leading causes of premature deaths and disability in the UK. People living in deprived areas of the UK are more likely to experience poor health outcomes, linked to many social determinants of health such as diet, housing, employment, education, power and discrimination and psycho-social factors such as isolation, quality of social network and perceived level of control.

pmc-12931306.title: Dynamic lysine acetylation and succinylation of platelet proteins regulates platelet storage lesion: mechanistic insights from multi-omics
pmc-12931306.creator: Xin Liao, Chenlu Zhang, Min Chen, Jianfeng Zhou, Xinpeng Luo, Yidan Zhang, Xingping Hu, Zhicheng Wang, Li Wang
pmc-12931306.description: ObjectivesPlatelet storage lesion (PSL) severely impairs platelet function during storage, presenting a major hurdle in transfusion medicine; however, the dynamic interplay between global proteomic changes and post-translational modifications (PTMs) underlying these functional deteriorations remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we report the first comprehensive multi-omics analysis integrating global proteomics, acetylomics, and succinylomics to dissect the molecular dynamics during platelet storage.

pmc-13188909.title: Association between relative handgrip strength and glycemic control among male automobile manufacturing workers using vibration tools in South Korea
pmc-13188909.creator: Dong-Jae Seo, Hyun Joong Kim, Yongjin Kim, Jaewon Mun, Jong-Han Leem, Shin-Goo Park, Dong-Wook Lee, Hwan-Cheol Kim
pmc-13188909.description: BackgroundAlthough the association between handgrip strength and glycemic control has been reported, studies conducted exclusively within specific occupational groups remain limited. To explore the association between handgrip strength and metabolic health in industrial settings, this study examined the relationship between relative handgrip strength and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) among male automobile manufacturing workers using vibration tools in South Korea.

pmc-13261596.title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries via Fused Impedance Feature and V‑Transformer-AGLU Network
pmc-13261596.creator: Yao Fang, Xuan Zhang, Yanchun Wang, Chunlan Yang, Chaolong Zhang, Anxiang Wang, Kaixin Cheng
pmc-13261596.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Accurate State of Health (SoH) estimation is critical to ensuring the safety and optimizing the performance of lithium-ion batteries. To address the limitations of existing methods in capturing the complex aging mechanisms and long-range temporal dependencies, this paper proposes a novel SoH estimation approach for lithium-ion batteries that integrates the Fused Impedance Feature (FIF) with a Vision Transformer embedded with an Adaptive Gated Linear Unit (V-Transformer-AGLU).

pmc-13450886.title: User Experience and Socioemotional Evaluation of Virtual Therapist Character Types in a Simulated Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy: Quantitative Study
pmc-13450886.creator: Michelle Celina Hallmann, Nicolina Laura Peperkorn, Francesco Vona, Youssef Shiban, Jan-Niklas Voigt-Antons, Ivan Steenstra
pmc-13450886.description: BackgroundVirtual reality exposure therapy (VRET) has emerged as an effective treatment for individuals with specific phobias, particularly for those unable to access traditional exposure therapy. However, several aspects of VRET applications still require further investigation, including the role of embodied conversational agents as virtual therapists.

uslaw-usc-t50-s208.title: 50 U.S.C. § 208 — Licensing or permitting commercial intercourse with State or region in insurrection
uslaw-usc-t50-s208.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t50-s208.description: United States Code, Title 50 (War And National Defense); Chapter 13 (Insurrection). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The President may, in his discretion, license and permit commercial intercourse with any part of such State or section, the inhabitants of which are so declared in a state of insurrection, so far as may be necessary to authorize supplying the necessities of loyal persons.
